parsed.explanation: Combined federal/division regime. Federal passport/visa screening treats sex by birth, restricts X, and may refuse entry, block/stranded documents or permanent fraud bars; immigration custody reports forced labour, solitary, beatings and sexual abuse. These traveler-facing federal exposures dominate and are not cancelled by the division. Inside the division, however, gender-identity anti-discrimination, no facility ban, courts, marker flexibility and care protections materially lower everyday and minor-related risk. Adult and guardian-with-minor exposure is high at entry/federal custody but more reduced post-admission; overall elevated-risk, not reduced.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal visa/entry screening checks sex assigned at birth, bars athletes, X-marker processing restrictions, discrepancy can cause refusal, evidence demand, passport block/stranding, fraud/permanent ineligibility; state protections do not offset border.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid until expiry; division public-accommodation protections reduce post-admission document friction; marker-change rules show institutional acceptance.
entry_documents.interaction: Local acceptance operates after admission; federal entry rules form initial universal barrier.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration/federal custody reports: trans men forced labour, gendered threats, beatings, solitary, severe sexual abuse; federal corrections adopt conversion-therapy practices; traveler detention possible from visa/document disputes.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Division correctional placement congruent (resident case) and anti-discrimination laws; no documented traveler-specific safe custody protocol.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Federal/immigration custody overrides local placement if border/visa incident occurs.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal/funded single-sex restrictions and federal facility rules may impose birth-sex placement at airports/federal sites; national map shows many state bans/criminal trespass, though not this division.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Division has no facility ban; 2014 court upheld bathroom alignment; anti-discrimination public accommodations.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State/federal funded facilities uncertain; local facilities safer, federal/funded settings create residual tier-1 exposure.

care_services.exposure: National rules threaten minor care, public insurance reimbursement, school investigations, hospital subpoenas, crisis-line shutdown; federal funding pressure.
care_services.protection: Division explicitly protects gender-affirming care, hormone therapy for 16/17, bans conversion therapy for minors, data collection.
care_services.interaction: Care in division protected, but national/minor and federal funding/investigation can chill; minor travelers face higher uncertainty.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal counterterrorism rewards and strategy name radical gender ideology/pro-trans groups as threat; entry fraud framing; foreign advisories.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Division hate-crime enhancements, anti-bias statutes, panic defence abolished; courts enforced protections.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Federal threat framing can shape border/visa/investigation; local law enforcement generally protective but cannot cure federal.

minors_guardians.exposure: National orders criminalize teachers facilitating social transition, block school funding, target minors' care; entry/federal screening; university sports compliance; sanctuary not enacted.
minors_guardians.protection: Division protects school bathroom access, care, marker updates, no facility ban; guardian can access care locally.
minors_guardians.interaction: Family/minor risk highest at border and federal schools/funded programs; local protections reduce day-to-day school/care.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No division-specific violence data; national hostility poll and federal framing suggest baseline risk; absence of incidents not safety.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Division anti-discrimination/hate-crime laws, court precedent, low-risk assessment, protections for public spaces.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Local state response may protect victims; federal/police encounters still risk profiling.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Federal courts unresolved, waiver rare, border/immigration discretion opaque; no data on division-specific enforcement against visitors or current facility preemption.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Division human-rights commission, hate-crime enhancements, court wins, FAQ on docs; state data mandates improve consistency.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies strongest locally; weakest at federal entry/custody. Unknowns affect enforcement frequency.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar to 0.35-B in border/document humiliation and discretionary exclusion, but worse in documented immigration-custody abuse. Division protections raise everyday safety above 0.35; overall near but below due federal custody and fraud bars.

0.45-D has universal registration exposure; our case has federal document screening but stronger local anti-discrimination, facility and care protections. Federal custody abuse and border discretion make it somewhat less safe than 0.45-D despite protective division.

Much safer than 0.75-C: there, border officers trained and detention brief/remedied. Here, passport/visa mismatch can strand, fraud bar, and immigration custody severe; local protections do not cure federal stage, so lower.

Far safer than 0.15-A: no presentation-specific criminal statute, capital ambiguity, or routine long pretrial custody for visitors. But federal custody and entry/fraud consequences keep it below 0.40+.

parsed.synthesis: Federal screening and immigration custody set severe tier-1 exposure at border and detention, independent of local acceptance. Within the division, gender-identity anti-discrimination, no facility ban, courts, marker flexibility, and minor-care protections substantially reduce street, service, health and guardian risks. Unknown enforcement frequency and federal facility/funding interactions leave residual high-risk, especially for minors or anyone detained.
